name: qsv-synthesize
description: Generate a synthetic CSV that is statistically faithful to a source CSV. Runs `stats` + `frequency` on the source so synthesized columns reproduce its per-column attributes — frequency-weighted sampling for categorical columns, quantile-bucketed numeric/date generation (quartiles by default), null-ratio preservation. With a Data Dictionary from `describegpt --dictionary --infer-content-type`, semantic Content Types pick realistic fake-rs fakers (names, emails, addresses, UUIDs, etc.) for non-enumerable columns. A dictionary `relationships` array preserves inter-column structure within each row — `joint` (functional dependencies like city/state/zip), `ordered` (monotonic chains like created_date ≤ closed_date) and `correlated` (numeric correlation via a Gaussian copula). Fully reproducible with `--seed`. Output is not anonymized: it can contain real source values, though by default values and `joint` tuples seen fewer than 5 times are dropped from the real values it samples, and numeric/date range ends are trimmed so a lone outlier can't set them (`--min-count`). `--report` writes a JSON summary of how many synthetic rows exactly match a source row (numbers and dates compared by value) and which values and `joint` tuples `--min-count` dropped.

args.name: input
args.description: The source CSV to profile. Omitted with --model, which generates from a saved model instead.

options.description: For structured-faker columns with bounded cardinality (cardinality fully captured by `frequency`), build a stable source-value -> fake-value mapping so the same source value always produces the same fake in the output. Preserves the source frequency distribution and overrides the default "emit real values when frequency-enumerated" behavior for structured fakers (names, emails, addresses, etc.). Has no effect on unstructured columns (lorem_*, free_text, unknown), all-unique columns, or non-faker columns. Useful for deidentified synthesis where you want stable joins on the faked columns.
Minimum absolute Spearman correlation for a pair of columns to stay in a `correlated` relationship. Weakly-correlated members are dropped.
The field delimiter for reading the input CSV. Must be a single character. (default: ,)

Data Dictionary JSON file produced by `describegpt --dictionary --infer-content-type --format JSON`. Layers semantic Content Types onto generation. If omitted, generation is purely type/frequency-based.

Output format: csv, jsonl or parquet. JSONL and Parquet keep each column's type: integers and floats as such, dates as Parquet dates (JSONL writes them as strings), empty values as null. A true/false column is written as booleans only if stats types it Boolean (pass it the option `--infer-boolean` via --stats-options); else it is text. A column sampled from real values keeps the type stats gave it only if every value converts unchanged, so a zero-padded code stays text. Parquet needs --output and a qsv built with the polars feature.

Frequency pool depth passed to the internal `frequency` run as --limit. A column is reproduced via exact frequency-weighted sampling only when its cardinality is fully captured within this limit; higher values reproduce more columns verbatim. 0 means unlimited.
Generate the Data Dictionary on the fly by invoking `describegpt --dictionary --infer-content-type` on <input>. Requires an LLM API key (QSV_LLM_APIKEY). Ignored if --dictionary is given.
Maximum number of distinct value-tuples a `joint` relationship may have. A joint group above this cap falls back to independent generation (or aborts under --strict-relationships). 0 means unlimited.

Locale for faker-backed columns. Case-insensitive. Supported: en, fr_fr, de_de, it_it, pt_br, pt_pt, ja_jp, zh_cn, zh_tw, ar_sa, cy_gb, fa_ir, nl_nl, tr_tr. Sparse locales (those without per-category data in fake-rs) silently fall back to en data for the missing categories — e.g. lorem text under a non-en locale is still English, since only zh_cn has localized lorem data.

Privacy threshold. A real value of an enumerated column, or a real `joint` value-tuple, that occurs fewer than <k> times in <input> is dropped from the values it samples; its share is redistributed over the kept values. An enumerated column whose values are all below <k> falls back to its faker or type-based generator (numeric and date columns to their trimmed range), and a joint group to independent columns, or aborts under the --strict-relationships option. A warning is printed when either happens. 1 disables suppression. Counts are of rows, not people: where one person has many rows (transactions, visits, logs), one person's value can pass <k> alone. Raise <k>, or dedupe to one row per person first. Numeric and date ranges, and the gaps of `ordered` relationships, are also trimmed to their k-th smallest and k-th largest values (one extra pass over <input>). A numeric or date column with fewer than 2k-1 non-null values is left empty unless its real values are sampled.

Generate from a model saved with --save-model instead of profiling an input, which must then be omitted. The model fixes everything fitted from the input, so options that shape the fit or read the input are refused when they have no default (for example the --dictionary, --stats-options, the --report and --delimiter options) and ignored when they do (for example the --locale, the --min-count and the frequency limit).
Disable inter-column relationship modeling. Every column is generated independently even when the dictionary declares a `relationships` array.
Write output to <file> instead of stdout.

Number of equal-share buckets that reproduce the shape of numeric and date columns: 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50 or 100. More buckets keep skewed and long-tailed columns closer to the source. 4 (the default) cuts at the source quartiles; other values cut at `stats --percentiles` (real source values). A column with too few non-null values for every bucket to hold more than <k> of them (<k> is set by the --min-count option) gets fewer buckets, or the quartiles. Also applies to the gaps of `ordered` relationships.

Write a JSON report of what the run reproduced from <input>: source and synthetic row counts, how many synthetic rows exactly match a source row (numbers and dates compared by value, other columns as text), and the values and joint tuples dropped by the --min-count option. Takes one extra pass over <input> and holds a hash per distinct source row in memory. A row with a float, free-text or faker column rarely matches exactly, so a low match rate does not by itself show that the output is private. A joint group that falls back to independent columns is listed, and so is each of its columns that also drops values, so suppressed rows can be counted more than once. Must not be the input, dictionary or output file.
Number of synthetic rows to generate.

Also save the fitted model to <file>, so later runs can generate from it with --model without reading <input> again. A --model run with the same --rows and --seed writes the same rows as this run (pools of fake values are sized for this run's --rows). The model holds real values from <input>, some of which the output may never show (see the privacy note above), so share it at least as carefully as the output. Its format is internal to qsv and versioned: a qsv that reads another model version refuses it, and it must be fitted again.

RNG seed for fully reproducible output. The same seed gives the same rows at any --jobs, unless stats uses approximate estimators: either asked for via --stats-options (e.g. `--quantile-method approx`), or switched on by stats itself (with a warning) when the input won't fit in memory.

Generate only slice k of N (k from 1 to N) of the rows --rows asks for. Requires --seed. Each slice is a run of whole 8192-row blocks, and slices 1 to N joined in order are the same as one unsharded run: CSV slices with `qsv cat rows`, JSONL slices by plain concatenation, while Parquet slices are separate files to read together as one dataset. Every slice must use the same <input>, options, qsv version and dictionary file, if any (--infer-content-type without --dictionary is refused). Each slice still profiles all of <input> itself, so if stats or frequency warns on one machine that it switched to approximate estimators for lack of memory, that slice comes from a different fit and the joined rows won't match one run. Generating the slices from one model saved with --save-model avoids this. Each CSV slice gets a header row (and each Parquet slice its schema) even when it has no rows (when N exceeds the number of blocks). The counts of --report are for this slice only.

Extra options appended to the internal `stats` run. Note: cardinality, quartiles and date inference are always enabled — do not re-specify them here. Column selection (--select/-s) and --weight are rejected; run `qsv select` on <input> first.
Abort instead of warning-and-degrading when a declared relationship fails validation.

Generate the other columns conditionally on the class of column <col> (a column name; with no headers, its 0-based index), e.g. a label to train a classifier on. Each row first draws a class by its share of the rows of <input>, then fills every other column from that class's own profile, so each column keeps its distribution within each class. A column with at most 50 distinct (trimmed) values is split by value, an empty value being a class of its own; a numeric column with more is split by its quantile buckets (see --quantiles), each class drawn at the share of rows its bucket holds (with tied bucket edges, not the shares of an ordinary fit), and any other column is refused. A class seen in fewer than <k> rows (<k> is set by the --min-count option) is dropped and its share redistributed. Fake-value columns, and columns a class has too few values to profile, use the generator fitted on the whole input. A numeric or date column needs at least 2k-1 values in a class, so with the default <k> of 5 a class of fewer than 9 rows takes all of them from the whole input; lower the --min-count to profile small classes, if that is acceptable for privacy. Relationships that name <col> drop it from their members, as do fake-value columns in the classes, and each class fits (and with --strict-relationships, enforces) them on its own rows. `stats` and `frequency` run once more per class, on a temporary copy of <input> split by class.
